rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: the maintainer note is the record a future session will trust to know commitment #11 is covered without re-checking; a false 'covered' record lets a real coverage hole (M6) go unnoticed indefinitely, which is exactly the 'most expensive error to catch late' this rule exists to prevent. Harm is present, not hypothetical — verified against shipped files. The maintainer block (L67) states verbatim: 'the strategy doc's commitment #11 is carried by M1, the M2 lecture and M6.' Checked all three against the strategy doc's own ledger (row #11, L897: home = 'M1, M2 lecture, M4 send-off, M6 callout') and against shipped curriculum: (a) M1 — CONFIRMED, `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/multi-session-git.md` L5 carries the line near-verbatim ('You do not have to start here. Find your way to this over time. There is no rush'), matching strategy-doc L301's quoted beat almost word for word. (b) M2 lecture — THIN BUT PRESENT: `curriculum/lectures/when-a-plan-is-good.md` L14 ('While Claude plans, other sessions could be making progress elsewhere. Not today, but soon' — tagged 'parallel-sessions-plant · none-owed' at L157) is the only session-adjacent line in that file; it plants parallel-sessions but withholds rather than grants permission, a weaker instance of #11 than the strategy doc's specified framing. (c) M6 — NOT FOUND: no file in the shipped M6 set (`spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md`, `composing-the-workflow.md`, `the-map-filled-in.md`, `agents-that-build-agents.md`, `reading-the-return.md`) contains any multisession-permission or worktrees-callout line. The strategy doc's planned carrier (L491, 'Worktrees callout at M6 scheduled-agents section') appears to have been dropped along with the 2026-07-05 cut of the 'Steering the wiring' lecture (`spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` L173) without the permission line being re-homed elsewhere in M6. Net: the note claims three carriers deliver the commitment; one is solid, one is thin, one does not exist in the shipped file set. The M4 cut itself is out of scope per standing ruling — this finding is about the note's overclaim on M6, not the cut.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Amend the maintainer note to name the actual state — M1 solid, M2 lecture thin/adjacent, M6 currently absent — or author the missing M6 line before claiming it carries #11; this is the strategy doc's / maintainer's bookkeeping to fix, not this file's body.
